newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Algerian helicopter heads to pick up Branson.
newsitem.headline: Algerian helicopter heads to pick up Branson.

text.p: An Algerian helicopter was on its way to pick up British tycoon Richard Branson and his co-pilots after the men landed in Algeria on Wednesday morning, aborting their attempt to fly round the world by balloon.
"They have come down not far from Bechar. They are in one piece, thank goodness," British ambassador to Algiers Jean-Francois Gordon said by telephone.
Bechar lies some 70 km (45 miles) inside Algeria from the border with Morocco from where Branson, Per Lindstrand and Alex Ritchie took off on Tuesday.

"The Algerians have been very, very good in helping us with this," Gordan said, adding that the Bechar area, about 480 km (300 miles) southwest of the city of Oran, was a good flat area for such a landing.
The three men, who were forced to land because of technical problems, were expected to be taken to Bechar and later to Algiers.
Earlier, the Virgin Global Challenger control centre in London said the balloon landed at 0729 GMT in the Algerian desert.
"The eagle has landed. No damage to capsule," Branson told his project team in London.
Officials said the problems that caused the project to be abandoned seemed to stem from the ratio of ballast to helium in the balloon.
